documentation.value:
-- Name -- Area variation
-- Definition -- The area variation during the evolution. This attribute has to be populated only if the type is "change".

-- Name -- Date
-- Definition -- The date when the change occured.

-- Name -- Evolution type
-- Definition -- The type of evolution.

-- Name -- Population variation
-- Definition -- The population variation during the evolution. This attribute has to be populated only if the type is "change".

constraint.name: AggregationConstraint
constraint.description: /* An evolution with a typeValue "aggregation" shall have at least two initial unit versions (the units to be aggregated) and a single final one (the resulting aggregation). */

constraint.name: ChangeConstraint
constraint.description: /* An evolution with a typeValue "change" shall have one initial unit version and one final one. */

constraint.name: ConsistencyConstraint
constraint.description: /* Evolution representations shall be consistent with the versions of the concerned objects. */

constraint.name: CreationConstraint
constraint.description: /* An evolution with a typeValue "creation" shall not have any initial unit versions and only one final one. */

constraint.name: DeletionConstraint
constraint.description: /* An evolution with a typeValue "deletion" shall have one initial unit version and no final one. */

constraint.name: SplittingConstraint
constraint.description: /* An evolution with a typeValue "splitting" shall have a single initial unit version (the unit to split), and at least two final ones (the units resulting from the splitting). */

constraint.name: AreaStatisticalUnitsConstraint
constraint.description: /* Vector statistical units with a reference geometry instance of GM_MultiSurface must be instances of the specialised class AreaStatisticalUnit. */

properties.documentation:
-- Name -- Vector statistical unit geometry
-- Definition -- A geometrical representation for vector statistical units.
-- Description -- Vector statistical units can have several representations depending on the context they are used for. It is adviced to produce at least one reference geometry.
EXAMPLE1: A vector statistical units may be represented both by an area and a point geometry. Such point can be the center of gravity or a label location.
EXAMPLE2: For mapping, different generalised representations of vector statistical units are required. These geometries depend on the visualisation scale.
